name: Transient erythroblastopenia of childhood
aliases: Transient red cell aplasia of childhood

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Transient erythroblastopenia of childhood diagnostic criteria

criteria.description: Bone marrow showing marked erythroid hypoplasia with normal myeloid and megakaryocytic lineages
Exclusion of other causes of anemia such as congenital pure red cell aplasia (Diamond-Blackfan anemia) and aplastic anemia
Spontaneous recovery of erythropoiesis within weeks to months

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of normocytic normochromic anemia with reticulocytopenia, bone marrow erythroid hypoplasia, and exclusion of other causes of red cell aplasia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and hematological; bone marrow biopsy is often required to confirm erythroid hypoplasia.

laboratory: Normal white blood cell and platelet counts
Bone marrow erythroid hypoplasia with normal myeloid and megakaryocytic lines
genetic: No known consistent genetic mutations; not inherited
other: Spontaneous resolution within weeks to months without specific treatment

distinguishingFeatures: Detection of parvovirus B19 DNA or IgM antibodies
Transient aplastic crisis in patients with hemolytic anemia

redFlags: Persistent pancytopenia beyond expected recovery period
Severe bleeding or bruising suggestive of thrombocytopenia
Signs of bone marrow failure such as infections or neutropenia
